novel_features.name: Point-in-polygon signal binding
novel_features.description: Bind a coordinate (or a CSV of coordinates) to the containing feature via one intersects query.
novel_features.rationale: Only possible because we issue a spatial intersects query and join locally instead of fuzzy address matching.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to attach a lat/lng distress signal to the exact parcel polygon that contains it.

novel_features.name: Service field audit
novel_features.description: Walk every layer in a service and report which high-value fields (owner, mailing address, homestead, last-sale) each layer exposes.
novel_features.rationale: Requires walking all layer schemas and comparing them locally, which no single API call returns.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to see which distress-signal fields a county actually exposes before building a load.

novel_features.name: Attribute change detection
novel_features.description: Re-query a layer and diff a tracked field against the last local sync to surface changes.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a local SQLite baseline from a prior sync; the API has no change feed.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to catch ownership/value changes between pulls without a deed scraper.

novel_features.name: Bbox tiling for capped layers
novel_features.description: Auto-subdivide the query envelope into quadrants when a layer exceeds the transfer limit and lacks pagination.
novel_features.rationale: Recursive local tiling around per-tile counts; incumbents silently truncate these layers.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this on large layers that return exceededTransferLimit but do not support resultOffset paging.

novel_features.name: Server-side stats passthrough
novel_features.description: Get counts/sums grouped by a field via outStatistics without downloading rows.
novel_features.rationale: Pushes aggregation to the server; combined with local store it beats pull-then-count.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this for per-category aggregates (parcels per land-use, acreage by owner) without a full pull.

novel_features.name: Offline SQL over synced layers
novel_features.description: Run SQLite/FTS queries over a synced layer's attributes with no further API calls.
novel_features.rationale: Only possible because sync mirrors features into a local store.
novel_features.example: arcgis-pp-cli sql "SELECT json_extract(attributes,'$.FLD_ZONE') AS zone, count(*) c FROM features GROUP BY zone ORDER BY c DESC"
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to slice a synced layer locally and compose with jq. Requires a prior sync.

narrative.headline: Point it at any ArcGIS FeatureServer or MapServer URL and pull, discover, or spatially bind features, with correct pagination, CSV/GeoJSON output, and a local store no other ArcGIS tool keeps.
narrative.value_prop: Every incumbent dumps one layer to GeoJSON and stops. This CLI discovers whole service directories, introspects layer schemas, does point-in-polygon signal binding, keeps an offline SQLite mirror you can SQL and diff, and outputs CSV straight into a data loader. Works anonymously against public endpoints; optional ArcGIS token for secured layers.

quickstart.comment: confirm the CLI is wired before hitting a live server
see a layer's fields, geometry type, and maxRecordCount
how many rows before you pull
pull matching features, paginated, to CSV

troubleshoots.fix: the layer hit maxRecordCount; query paginates automatically — if the server lacks resultOffset support, add --tile
add --tile to subdivide the envelope, or --pager oid to force OBJECTID chunking
the layer is secured; pass --token or set ARCGIS_TOKEN

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI to pull, discover, or spatially query any ArcGIS REST FeatureServer/MapServer — county parcels, code-enforcement, permits, flood zones. It is the right tool when you need correct pagination, CSV/GeoJSON for a data loader, an offline mirror, or point-in-polygon binding of a coordinate to its containing feature.
anti_triggers: Do not use it to render maps or tiles — it extracts and queries data, not imagery.
Do not use it for non-Esri OGC/WFS endpoints; it speaks the ArcGIS REST query protocol specifically.

recipes.title: Pull matching features to CSV
recipes.explanation: Paginated pull, only the fields you need.

recipes.title: Bind a coordinate to its containing polygon
recipes.explanation: One intersects query returns the containing feature; --select narrows the response.

recipes.title: Audit a service's fields before a load
recipes.explanation: Reports which high-value fields each layer exposes.

recipes.title: Detect changes since last sync
recipes.explanation: Diffs a tracked field against the local sync baseline (run sync first).
